question: Provide a brief company overview.
answer: Tallyhouse CRM, Inc. was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas. We employ about 420 people and serve roughly 1,900 customers, including 150 public-sector organizations, on a single CRM and service platform.

question: How many employees does your company have?
answer: Tallyhouse has about 420 full-time employees as of Q3 2026, including about 60 in professional services and 45 in customer support.

question: How many customers use your platform?
answer: About 1,900 organizations use Tallyhouse: roughly 1,750 commercial customers and 150 public-sector customers, including cities, counties and universities.

question: Describe your company's financial stability.
answer: Tallyhouse is a privately held, venture-backed company (Series C) with annual recurring revenue of about $62 million. Audited financial statements can be shared under NDA during final evaluation.

question: Is your company publicly traded?
answer: No. Tallyhouse is privately held.

question: Where is your company headquartered, and where are staff who access customer data located?
answer: Headquarters is in Austin, Texas. All support and services staff who access customer data are based in the United States.

question: How long has your company provided this solution?
answer: Tallyhouse has provided its CRM platform since 2017 and the Public Sector Edition since 2020.

question: Has your company been involved in litigation or had contracts terminated in the last five years?
answer: No. Tallyhouse has no pending material litigation and has had no contracts terminated for cause in the last five years.

question: Describe your proposed solution.
answer: The Tallyhouse Platform is a cloud CRM with Sales, Service, Marketing, Operations and Analytics modules built on one shared data model. Every contact, organization, case and activity lives on a single record, so teams see the full history of each relationship.

question: Does the system provide a single record for each customer or constituent?
answer: Yes. Every module shares one data model, so a contact's cases, emails, requests, deals and notes appear on one record.

question: Can the system manage cases or tickets with SLA tracking?
answer: Yes. The Service module tracks cases with configurable SLA timers, escalation rules and breach alerts. SLA performance appears on standard dashboards.

question: Does the solution include a knowledge base?
answer: Yes. The Service module includes internal and public knowledge bases with article versioning, an approval workflow and search.

question: Can users attach documents to records?
answer: Yes. Users can attach Word, PDF, Excel, image and other common files to any record, up to 100 MB per file.

question: Can administrators configure workflows without code?
answer: Yes. The Operations module provides a visual workflow builder for routing, notifications, field updates and approvals, with no coding required.

question: Does the system support custom fields and custom objects?
answer: Custom fields are available on all plans. Custom objects are available on the Enterprise plan and the Public Sector Edition, not on Professional.

question: Describe your reporting and dashboard capabilities.
answer: The Analytics module includes standard dashboards, a drag-and-drop report builder, scheduled email reports and CSV or Excel export. Business users can build custom reports without IT help.

question: Is a mobile app available?
answer: Yes. Native iOS and Android apps are available to staff, and the Public Sector Edition includes a resident-facing mobile app.

question: Does the system include email marketing and newsletter tools?
answer: Yes. The Marketing module supports email campaigns, newsletters, forms, landing pages and segmentation, with consent tracking.

question: Does the system detect and merge duplicate records?
answer: Yes. The Operations module flags likely duplicates using configurable matching rules and lets admins merge them while keeping the full activity history.

question: How often is the software updated, and is there downtime?
answer: Tallyhouse releases updates every two weeks with no customer downtime. Major changes are announced 30 days in advance in release notes.

question: Does the solution include AI features, and is our data used to train models?
answer: Yes. Optional AI features summarize cases, suggest knowledge articles and draft emails. Customer data is not used to train shared models, and admins can turn AI features off for the account.

question: Does the platform provide sales forecasting?
answer: Yes. The Sales module provides pipeline stages, weighted forecasts and forecast categories by rep, team and period.

question: Does the solution support 311-style service requests?
answer: Yes. The Public Sector Edition is built for 311-style request intake, routing, tracking and closure across departments.

question: Which channels can residents use to submit requests?
answer: Residents can submit requests through the web portal, the iOS and Android apps, SMS and email, or by phone through the agent console used by city staff.

question: Can residents track the status of their requests?
answer: Yes. Each request receives a tracking number. Residents can check status online or receive SMS and email updates without creating an account.

question: Can requests be routed by department, district or location?
answer: Yes. Routing rules assign requests by request type, department, council district or map location, and reassign them automatically when a rule changes.

question: Does the system include GIS mapping?
answer: Yes, through a native integration with Esri ArcGIS. Requests are geocoded, shown on maps and can be routed by GIS layers such as districts or service zones.

question: Can council members track constituent issues in their district?
answer: Yes. Council offices can view, assign and report on constituent cases by district, with dashboards for open issues and response times.

question: Is there a limit on resident or portal users?
answer: No. The Public Sector Edition includes unlimited resident records and portal users. Pricing is based on staff users only.

question: Do you hold a cooperative purchasing contract?
answer: No. Tallyhouse does not currently hold a cooperative purchasing contract and responds to each solicitation directly.

question: What integrations are available out of the box?
answer: Native integrations include Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Esri ArcGIS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Twilio, DocuSign, QuickBooks and NetSuite. The app marketplace lists more than 300 additional integrations.

question: Do you provide an open API?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse provides a documented REST API covering all standard and custom objects, plus webhooks for real-time events.

question: What are your API rate limits?
answer: Enterprise accounts may make 150 requests per 10 seconds. Bulk endpoints are available for large data loads.

question: Does the system integrate with Microsoft 365 email and calendar?
answer: Yes. The native Microsoft 365 integration syncs email, calendar events and contacts with Tallyhouse records.

question: Does the system support single sign-on?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse supports SSO through SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect, including Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.
tags: SSO, SAML, OIDC, Okta, Entra ID

question: Does the solution include built-in telephony or a contact center?
answer: Not natively. Tallyhouse integrates with Twilio and with existing phone systems through telephony partners, so agents can log calls and see caller records in the agent console.

question: Can data be imported and exported in bulk?
answer: Yes. Admins can import and export records by CSV, and the bulk API supports scheduled loads. Customers can export all of their data at any time.

question: Can the system integrate with our ERP or financial system?
answer: Native integrations exist for QuickBooks and NetSuite. Other ERP systems connect through the REST API or integration platforms such as MuleSoft or Workato.

question: Does the system integrate with e-signature tools?
answer: Yes. The native DocuSign integration sends documents for signature from any record and stores the signed copy back on that record.

question: Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse completes an annual SOC 2 Type II audit covering security, availability and confidentiality. The current report is available under NDA.

question: Are you ISO 27001 certified?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse is certified to ISO/IEC 27001. The certificate is available on request.

question: Are you FedRAMP authorized?
answer: No. Tallyhouse is not FedRAMP authorized and does not currently pursue federal agency deployments.

question: Are you StateRAMP authorized?
answer: Not yet. Tallyhouse is in the StateRAMP authorization process, with a target of Q2 2027. Our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate are available now.

question: How is customer data encrypted?
answer: Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher. Encryption keys are managed in the cloud provider's key management service and rotated every year.

question: Do you support multi-factor authentication?
answer: Yes. MFA can be enforced for all users, and SSO customers can apply their identity provider's MFA policies.

question: Describe your role-based access controls.
answer: Admins assign users to roles that control access to objects, records and individual fields. Permissions can be limited by team, department or district.

question: Do you maintain audit logs?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse logs user and admin actions, including logins, record changes, exports and permission changes. Logs are kept for 12 months and can be exported.

question: How often do you perform penetration testing?
answer: An independent firm performs a penetration test every year. We also run quarterly vulnerability scans and a public bug bounty program. A summary of the latest test is available under NDA.
tags: penetration test, vulnerability scanning, bug bounty

question: Describe your incident response process.
answer: Tallyhouse maintains a documented incident response plan that is tested twice a year. Customers are notified within 72 hours of a confirmed breach affecting their data.

question: Will you sign a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement?
answer: No. Tallyhouse does not sign HIPAA BAAs, and the platform should not be used to store protected health information.

question: Are you CJIS compliant?
answer: No. Tallyhouse does not meet Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) requirements and should not be used to store criminal justice information.

question: Do employees receive security training and background checks?
answer: Yes. All employees complete security awareness training when hired and every year after, and pass background checks before they receive system access.

question: How do you manage third-party vendor risk?
answer: Tallyhouse reviews subprocessors before onboarding and every year, including security questionnaires and audit reports. The current subprocessor list is published on our trust page.

question: Do you encrypt data in transit?
answer: Yes. All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.0 or higher.

question: Where is the solution hosted?
answer: Customers choose AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud. Primary and disaster-recovery regions are both in the United States.
tags: hosting, cloud provider, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud

question: Is customer data stored only in the United States?
answer: Yes. All customer data, including backups, is stored in US regions.

question: What uptime do you guarantee?
answer: Tallyhouse guarantees 99.9% monthly uptime, excluding scheduled maintenance, with service credits if we fall short.

question: What are your RPO and RTO?
answer: The recovery point objective is 1 hour and the recovery time objective is 4 hours. Disaster recovery is tested twice a year.

question: How are backups handled?
answer: Backups run daily, are encrypted and are kept for 35 days in a separate US region.

question: Can the solution be hosted on-premises?
answer: No. Tallyhouse is offered only as a cloud service on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud. On-premises and private-cloud deployments are not available.

question: Which cloud provider do you use?
answer: Tallyhouse is hosted exclusively on AWS in us-east-1, with disaster recovery in us-west-2.

question: Can our data be hosted in the EU?
answer: Not currently. All data is stored in US regions. An EU region is planned for 2027.

question: Describe your implementation methodology.
answer: Implementations follow five phases: discovery and design, configuration, data migration, training, and launch with 30 days of hypercare. A Tallyhouse project manager leads each phase with a named customer counterpart.

question: How long does a typical implementation take?
answer: Commercial implementations take 8 to 12 weeks. Public Sector Edition implementations take 12 to 16 weeks, depending on the number of departments and integrations.

question: Who performs the implementation?
answer: Tallyhouse's own professional services team performs every implementation. We do not rely on third-party consultants.

question: How do you migrate data from our current system?
answer: We map your data during discovery, run two test loads for your team to validate, then perform the final migration before launch. Sources can include spreadsheets, legacy CRMs and databases.

question: What training do you provide?
answer: We provide admin training, end-user training and train-the-trainer sessions, delivered live online or on site. Recorded courses and a certification program are available at no extra cost.

question: How much customer staff time will the implementation need?
answer: Customers typically assign a project lead at about half of their time, plus subject-matter experts for a few hours a week during discovery and testing.

question: Is onsite support available during implementation?
answer: Yes. Onsite workshops and launch support are available. Travel is billed at cost unless it is included in the fixed-fee scope.

question: What happens after go-live?
answer: After 30 days of hypercare, the account moves to a customer success manager for quarterly business reviews, adoption planning and roadmap updates. Accounts over $50K ARR have a named customer success manager.

question: What support hours do you provide?
answer: Standard support runs Monday to Friday, 7am to 7pm Central. Premium support adds 24/7 coverage for P1 and P2 issues.

question: What are your support response times?
answer: Standard support responds to P1 issues within 4 hours. Premium responds within 1 hour, and Premium with a technical account manager within 30 minutes.

question: How do you define issue severity levels?
answer: P1: the service is down or unusable for most users. P2: a major feature is impaired with no workaround. P3: a feature is impaired but a workaround exists. P4: questions and feature requests.

question: Which support channels are available?
answer: Customers can reach support by phone, email, in-app chat and the support portal.

question: Will we have a dedicated account manager?
answer: Accounts over $50K ARR receive a named customer success manager. A named technical account manager is available as an add-on for accounts over $150K ARR.

question: Where is your support team located?
answer: All support staff are Tallyhouse employees based in the United States.

question: Describe your pricing model.
answer: Commercial plans are priced per user per month: Professional at $90 and Enterprise at $150. The Public Sector Edition is a $30,000 annual platform fee plus $1,200 per staff user per year.

question: Are implementation fees fixed or hourly?
answer: Implementation is a one-time fixed fee, typically $25,000 to $120,000, set during scoping.

question: Do you offer multi-year discounts?
answer: Yes. Two-year terms receive a 10% discount and three-year terms a 15% discount.

question: Are there additional costs for storage, API calls or upgrades?
answer: API access and all product upgrades are included. File storage up to 1 TB is included, and more is available as an add-on.

question: Are annual price increases capped?
answer: Yes. Renewal increases are capped at 5% per year for multi-year agreements.

question: What is the price of the Professional plan?
answer: The Professional plan is $80 per user per month.

question: Will you accept our standard contract terms?
answer: Tallyhouse will review your terms and has accepted most public-sector standard agreements with limited changes, mainly to liability and indemnity. Any proposed exceptions are listed in our response.

question: Who owns the customer data?
answer: The customer owns all of its data. Tallyhouse processes it only to provide the service and does not sell customer data.

question: What happens to our data when the contract ends?
answer: Customers can export all data at any time. After termination, data stays available for 30 days, is then deleted from production within 30 days and from backups within 35 days. A deletion certificate is available on request.

question: Do you comply with GDPR and CCPA?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse offers a GDPR-ready data processing agreement and supports CCPA requests, including access and deletion.

question: Do you carry cyber liability insurance?
answer: Yes. Tallyhouse carries $10 million in cyber liability coverage and $2 million in general liability coverage. Certificates of insurance are available on request.

question: How do you support public records requests?
answer: Tallyhouse supports customers' public records obligations through full data export and audit logs. Customers remain responsible for responding to public records requests.

question: Do you use subcontractors to deliver services?
answer: Tallyhouse does not subcontract implementation or support. Infrastructure is provided by the customer's chosen cloud provider, which is listed on our subprocessor page.

question: Does the solution meet WCAG 2.1 AA?
answer: Yes. The resident portal and mobile app meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, verified by an annual third-party audit. A VPAT is available on request.

question: Is the staff application accessible?
answer: The staff application supports keyboard navigation and screen readers. Full WCAG 2.1 AA conformance for the staff application is scheduled for Q1 2027.

question: Is the resident portal available in multiple languages?
answer: Yes. The resident portal and app are available in English and Spanish, with automatic translation for 30 more languages.

question: Provide three public-sector references.
answer: City of Harlow Springs (population 210,000), Meridian County (population 480,000) and Bellcrest University. Contact details are provided after shortlisting.

question: Describe a similar implementation and its results.
answer: The City of Harlow Springs launched the Public Sector Edition for 311 requests. Average request resolution time fell from 6.2 to 3.9 days in the first year.

question: What differentiates your solution from competitors?
answer: Tallyhouse combines public-sector features such as 311 intake, GIS routing and accessibility with a full CRM on one data model, and goes live in weeks with our own team rather than outside consultants.

question: Describe a commercial customer outcome.
answer: Ridgeway Logistics, a 900-employee company, moved its sales pipeline from spreadsheets to Tallyhouse. Forecast accuracy rose from 71% to 88%.

question: Describe a county-level implementation.
answer: Meridian County replaced three legacy systems with the Public Sector Edition and went live in 14 weeks.
